findings.finding: First failure is a test fixture incorrectly treating every one-shot nonblocking Busy as unexpected.
findings.reason: Pool::call submits one job, immediately panics on any rejected admission, and waits for result before next call. This particular material_hub test uses that pool serially without any other producer. The mailbox has 8 queued-job slots and4MiB budget; Job declares only3*64KiB plus small inline state. A completed previous task has already been dequeued. Under these constraints queued capacity/bytes cannot be exhausted by this test; Busy can arise when the same mailbox mutex is temporarily held by either original worker try_recv. Nonblocking lock contention is an explicit existing mailbox contract, not product pool corruption. The raw failure does not record which Pool::call invocation failed, so the exact schedule is not observed.

findings.finding: Second failure is UploadHubOwner global singleton Busy, not WorkerPool admission Busy.
findings.reason: The line calls UploadHubOwner::new().unwrap(). First material test already created an owner but did not reach pool.join and owner.drain_after_join at its end after the fixture admission panic. Owner Drop intentionally keeps the original Shared in fixed RETAINED and leaves OWNER=true whenever drained is false, even if logical slots happen to be empty. Pool Drop joining its workers alone does not set owner.drained. The later serialized Hub test therefore cannot create a replacement; this is the expected fail-closed cascade. No permission to discard the retained owner or infer physical release is implied by this diagnosis.

findings.finding: Ticket result delivery and physical worker/capacity return are distinct, but that distinction alone is not the admission cause here.
findings.reason: Success Completion.finish queues reply, then sets done and runs notification; Running drops after the successful branch returns. try_result or wait may observe the reply before done/running decrements. Even is_finished is not a promise of idle physical thread. However running is only accounting and is not consulted by try_submit: admission is mailbox try_send. Queue charge is removed on receiver pop before Task execution. Waiting for ticket.done/running0 cannot guarantee next nonblocking mailbox lock is uncontended; the other worker may hold it. Production metadata-only output/worker-owner contract is unchanged.
